extraction.name: MINT-1T: Scaling Open-Source Multimodal Data by 10x: A Multimodal Dataset with One Trillion Tokens
extraction.description: MINT-1T is the most extensive and diverse open-source Multimodal INTerleaved dataset to date, comprising one trillion text tokens and 3.4 billion images. It includes previously untapped sources such as PDFs and ArXiv papers, aiming to bridge the gap in multimodal training data between closed- and open-source models.
extraction.creator: Anas Awadalla, Le Xue, Oscar Lo, Manli Shu, Hannah Lee, Etash Guha, Matt Jordan, Sheng Shen, Mohamed Awadalla, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Ran Xu, Yejin Choi, Ludwig Schmidt
extraction.publisher: University of Washington, Salesforce Research, Stanford University, University of Texas at Austin, University of California, Berkeley
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data was sourced from CommonCrawl WARC and WAT dumps, and ArXiv S3 buckets. HTML documents were parsed from CommonCrawl WARC files. PDF documents were sourced from CommonCrawl WAT files. ArXiv documents were built from LaTeX source code. The data collection process involved software-based parsing, downloading, and filtering.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: None explicitly stated as missing; however, the dataset relies on external image URLs which may suffer from link rot, meaning images might not be available over time.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CommonCrawl WARC dumps (HTML), CommonCrawl WAT dumps (PDFs), and ArXiv LaTeX source code.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Data collected from January 2024 to June 2024. The underlying web data spans from May 2017 to April 2024 for HTML, February 2023 to April 2024 for PDFs, and the full history for ArXiv.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data was manipulated by parsing DOM trees for HTML, extracting reading order and images from PDFs using PyMuPDF, and interleaving images with text from ArXiv LaTeX using TexSoup. Documents were filtered for quality, deduplicated, and safety-checked.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing included: 1) Filtering out documents with no images or >30 images. 2) Removing NSFW content via URL substring filtering and image classification. 3) Anonymizing PII (emails, IPs). 4) Language identification (Fasttext) to keep only English. 5) Text quality filtering (MassiveText rules, duplicate n-grams). 6) Image filtering (size, aspect ratio, retrievability). 7) Deduplication using Bloom filters for text and SHA256 hashes for images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset is unlabeled and intended for pre-training. No human annotations or labels were created.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: PyMuPDF, TexSoup, Fasttext, MassiveText, Bloom Filter, SHA256, NSFW image detector (GantMan/nsfw_model)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released under CC-BY-4.0. Authors will actively respond to issues and maintain the dataset. Updates will be communicated via the Huggingface interface README. Older versions are available via Git history. A mechanism for opting out/removing samples is provided via a Google form.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains data from the public web which may include personally identifiable information (PII) such as names, faces, and locations. However, the authors explicitly removed email addresses and IP addresses. The dataset may still contain sensitive content if present on the public web.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to democratize access to large-scale multimodal data, reducing the disparity between open-source and closed-source models. It supports open science in multimodal model training.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases present in the CommonCrawl and ArXiv sources. The HTML subset is less biased towards specific domains compared to OBELICS, but PDFs are heavily skewed towards Science and Technology. The authors note that text quality filters might favor certain demographics, though they avoided model-based heuristics for this reason.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: 1) PDF parsing may result in incorrect reading orders or missed images due to arbitrary layouts. 2) The dataset is not self-contained as it relies on external image URLs which may rot. 3) It is not representative of all web content, being filtered by quality and safety. 4) It may still contain offensive or sensitive content despite filtering efforts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training large multimodal models (LMMs), specifically for pre-training on interleaved image-text sequences. It is not recommended for training models that ingest/generate PII or for military applications.
